findings.claim: Found by probing a completed copy (my own runbook edits). A print-one-api-setting value that does use exec on api, but with a compound or piped shell script, is rejected with the wrong message. Three examples: docker compose exec api sh -c "env | grep DATASOURCE", sh -c "echo $A; echo $B", and sh -c 'printenv X; env'. All three get "run the command inside the running api container, not in a new one", which names a rule the learner already met. The likely cause: the command parser returns no command for a line with ;, | or &&, and runbook-exec reports its first rule. The behaviour is the same at cb8c2e07, so this is not a loop-2 regression. Other runbook rules also give their own outcome message, not a format message, for a chained line (for example start-stack for "up -d && ps"). README line 222 says to write one command per key with no ;, &&, pipes or redirection, and line 277 says to read the message for the rule, so the learner is not blocked; but this message sends them to the wrong fix.

evidence.section: Phase 5 command format line and Troubleshooting runbook row

findings.recommendation: When an entry cannot be parsed as one docker or podman command (it contains ;, |, &&, || or redirection), return one format message naming the key, such as "<key>: write one command with no ;, &&, pipes or redirection", before the rule-specific checks. Apply it to every runbook rule.
